_meta.about: Registrations a Tamil Nadu startup may need, in order. Each step says who must do it (rules on the founder's facts), why, documents, the official place to do it, and typical time. Licences specific to a product come from the planner's regulatory library through the domain card.

confidence.official: read on the regulator's own site
confidence.secondary: well established; confirm details on the source
confidence.to_verify: likely applies; confirm with the authority before relying on it

entity.ask: How is the business set up: not registered yet, proprietorship, partnership, LLP, private limited company, or one-person company?

years_since_incorporation.ask: How many years ago was it registered?

turnover_lakh.ask: Roughly what yearly turnover do you expect, in lakh rupees?

interstate.ask: Will you sell goods to buyers in other states?

sells_online.ask: Will you sell through online marketplaces such as Amazon or Flipkart?

innovative.ask: Is the business built on a new or clearly better product, process or business model?

has_brand.ask: Will you sell under your own brand name?

has_premises.ask: Do you have a shop, office, factory or workshop?

employees.ask: How many people will you employ, not counting founders?

raise_equity.ask: Do you plan to raise money from investors for a share of the company?

steps.title: Choose the business structure
steps.why: The structure decides your liability, how you can raise money, and whether you qualify for startup recognition.

applies.label: the business is not registered yet

advice.text: A private limited company is the usual choice if you will raise investor money; investors buy shares.
An LLP has lower running compliance and still qualifies for startup recognition, but investors rarely fund LLPs.
A proprietorship is quickest, but it does not qualify for DPIIT startup recognition.

steps.title: Incorporate the company or LLP on the MCA portal
steps.why: Gives the business its own legal identity; company forms (SPICe+) can also apply for PAN, TAN, EPFO and ESIC registration and a bank account together.

all.label: you chose a company or LLP

documents: PAN and Aadhaar of every director or partner
Address proof of the registered office (rent agreement with owner's NOC, and a recent utility bill)
Digital signature certificates for directors or designated partners

steps.title: Register the partnership firm
steps.why: A registered partnership can sue to enforce contracts and qualifies for DPIIT recognition; an unregistered one cannot.
documents: Address proof of the place of business

steps.title: Open a current account in the business's name
steps.why: Keeps business money separate; banks, schemes and investors all ask for it.

steps.title: Udyam registration (MSME)
steps.why: Free and online. Unlocks MSME benefits: collateral-free loan guarantees (CGTMSE), priority-sector lending, many state schemes, and protection against buyers who pay late.
documents: Aadhaar of the owner, a partner or a director
PAN and GSTIN of the business (GSTIN where you have one)

steps.title: GST registration
steps.why: Needed to collect GST and to claim the GST you pay on inputs; business buyers and marketplaces usually need your GSTIN.

applies.label: compulsory above ₹40 lakh turnover for goods (₹20 lakh for services), for inter-state supply of goods, and for selling goods through online marketplaces

recommended.label: below the limits it is optional, but it lets you claim input tax and sell to businesses that want GST invoices

documents: Aadhaar and photos of the owners or directors
Address proof of the place of business

steps.title: Import Export Code
steps.why: Customs will not clear an export or import without it.

steps.title: DPIIT startup recognition
steps.why: Opens Startup India benefits: self-certification under several labour and environment laws, cheaper and faster patents and trademarks, relaxed rules in government tenders, and the route to tax holidays and fund-of-funds investors.

all.label: a private limited company, LLP or registered partnership (a proprietorship does not qualify)
turnover under ₹100 crore in every year
working on innovation, or a clearly better product, process or scalable business model

documents: A short write-up on what is new and how it creates jobs or wealth

steps.title: Register on StartupTN
steps.why: Tamil Nadu's startup mission: needed for TANSEED and other state support, incubator programmes and events.
documents: DPIIT recognition number, if you have it

steps.title: File a trademark for your brand name
steps.why: Stops others registering your name first; marketplaces need it for brand registry. Startups and small enterprises pay a lower fee.

applies.label: you sell under your own brand

documents: The classes of goods or services
Udyam or DPIIT certificate for the lower fee

steps.title: Shops and establishments registration (Tamil Nadu)
steps.why: Shops, offices and commercial establishments in Tamil Nadu register under the state's shops and establishments law.

applies.label: you have a shop, office or workshop

steps.title: Professional tax enrolment
steps.why: In Tamil Nadu the local body (corporation or municipality) levies professional tax on businesses and on salaries above set limits.

steps.title: ESIC registration
steps.why: Employee health insurance; compulsory once you employ 10 or more people (company forms can register at incorporation).

steps.title: EPFO registration (provident fund)
steps.why: Retirement savings for employees; compulsory once you employ 20 or more people.
